scenes.title: Home to Room Eight
scenes.summary: After settling the retired mapmaker happily at table one under the shade tree, F1, M2, and M3 step to the front desk to fetch the green guest book and brass key number 8.
scenes.intro: Warm applause ripples across the courtyard of {SHOW} as neighbours greet their honoured visitor under the shade tree. Inside at the front desk, {F1}, {M2}, and {M3} beam ear to ear as they fetch two special treasures to bring out to table one. Listen first.
story: M3
Did you see my old teacher beam when he saw the green shutters open, {M2}?!
M2
He recognized our old walnut piano through the glass before he took three steps!
F1
And he remembered your name right on the station platform, did he not, {M3}?
M3
Called me Front-Row Notebook before I even lowered the compass welcome sign!
M2
He whispered that his voice is hoarse from talking on the long train ride.
F1
No wonder he patted his coat pocket—he brought a toast card for us!
M2
First let me bring out my family green guest book opened to May thirty years ago.
F1
And may we lend him brass key number eight from the wooden board for the afternoon?
M2
Room Eight is empty tonight—better yet, {F1}, Room Eight is his on the house!
M3
He also handed {M4} a flat wooden parcel wrapped in brown kraft paper at the gate.
F1
Oooh, a flat parcel from a master mapmaker? Do not peek until after cake!
M2
Carry out the brass compass and key number eight—Room Nine is ready for music!
scenes.outro: Called Front-Row Notebook on the platform, {M3} beams as Room 8 is gifted on the house for the night! See you in the café corner next time.

scenes.title: Slices of Summer Cake
scenes.summary: At the bustling café counter, F2 plates generous slices of berry-and-almond cake while M4 and F1 report that the honoured guest called it identical to thirty summers ago.
scenes.intro: At the cheerful café counter, {F2} cuts golden ruby-topped slices of summer berry-and-almond cake onto stoneware plates while {F1} and {M4} hurry back with empty trays and shining eyes. Let us listen in first.
story: F2
Tell me everything right now—did table one taste the berry almond cake yet?!
M4
He took one small bite, closed both eyes, and tapped his hand over his heart!
F1
Then he nodded twice to {M2} and wrote two words on his napkin: Exact match!
F2
EXACT MATCH! Did you hear that, kitchen ovens?! Honey and orange zest won the day!
M4
Number ten from next door said it tastes like May afternoon sunshine thirty years back.
F1
And every single neighbour clipped their numbered birch clothespin onto their lapel like a badge!
F2
Even that soggy poster accident turned into the hit fashion trend of {STREET}!
M4
Here go six more slices for table three—save two big corners for the musicians!
F1
Listen—{F3} and {M3} just sat down side by side on the walnut piano bench!
F2
Turn down the tea kettle burner so the whole courtyard hears every single note!
M4
Come stand by the archway with us, {F2}—the ovens earned a five-minute break!
F2
Wiping my hands right now—play us home, Room Nine!
scenes.outro: Two words on a napkin—Exact match—crown {F2}'s kitchen triumph just as four hands touch the walnut piano keys! See you inside Room 9 next time.

scenes.title: The Four-Hand Duet
scenes.summary: Inside Room 9, F3 and M3 perform their joyful four-hand piano duet through the open shutters to warm applause from all twenty-eight courtyard seats.
scenes.intro: Golden afternoon light slants through the open green shutters of Room 9 as {F3} and {M3} finish the lively final bars of their four-hand piano duet while {F1} listens beside the doorway. Listen first.
story: F3
Softly into the bridge now, {M3}... let the bass notes walk like gentle footsteps.
M3
Breathing first, answering second—right up to middle D together!
F1
Look out under the shade tree: not a single teacup is clinking anywhere!
F3
Here comes our bright final scale to the top—one, two, three, and hold!
F1
BRAVO! Listen to all twenty-eight chairs clapping across the courtyard stones!
M3
{F3}, I did not rush bar sixteen—and I forgot all about counting metres!
F3
You played like a true musician, {M3}, and look who is standing up at table one!
F1
Your old professor is lifting his teacup high toward the sunroom window!
M3
And he is waving {F1} and {M2} over to open that brown paper parcel!
F3
Go on out under the lanterns, both of you—I am right behind you.
F1
Here is the ivory toast card he asked us to read to the courtyard!
M3
Thirty summers between two songs—and the courtyard sounds warmer than ever.
scenes.outro: Four hands at one rescued piano bring the whole courtyard to its feet, and now the flat brown parcel awaits under the tree! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Illustrated Map Gift
scenes.summary: Under the shade tree, F1 reads the retired mapmaker's warm written toast aloud while M2 and F2 unveil his gift: a framed watercolour map of {STREET} with {SHOW} glowing at its centre.
scenes.intro: Beneath the old shade tree, {M2} and {F2} untie the twine on the flat brown parcel at table one while {F1} steps forward to read the hoarse mapmaker's handwritten toast card aloud to the smiling neighbours. Listen first.
story: F1
Friends of {STREET}, forgive my tired train-ride voice and let {F1} share my thanks.
M2
Read loud and clear so the back tables by the fountain basin hear too, {F1}!
F1
Thirty Mays ago, a rainy week trapped a young traveller inside Room Eight.
F2
That was the exact week your aunt poured hot tea and started the sunroom waltz!
F1
Listen: I spent thirty years drawing great cities, yet no place ever felt warmer than here.
M2
Lift away the brown wrapping paper with me on three, {F2}—one, two, three!
F2
OH! Look at the walnut frame—it is a giant hand-painted map of {STREET}!
F1
There is the stone fountain, the clock tower, the bookshop arch, and the park bench!
M2
And right in the middle, painted in warm gold leaf, sits {SHOW} and Room Nine!
F2
Look at the tiny figures he painted in our courtyard—someone even has forehead glasses!
M2
Hey! That distinguished gentleman by the gate is remarkably handsome, thank you very much!
F1
Let us hang this map right beside hook number nine so no traveller ever gets lost!
scenes.outro: Painted in watercolour and gold leaf, {STREET} and {SHOW} shine inside a walnut frame—complete with tiny forehead glasses! See you next time.

scenes.title: A New Tin for Tomorrow
scenes.summary: As early evening settles in, M1 surprises F1 inside Room 9 with a brand-new brass-rimmed tin box and waxed linen to seal a new time capsule for thirty summers ahead.
scenes.intro: As twilight turns the rooftop-to-tree lanterns golden outside, {M1} quietly calls {F1} into Room 9, where a gleaming new blue-and-brass square tin sits beside fresh yellow waxed cloth. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: F1
{M1}! Where did this shining blue-and-brass tin box come from?!
M1
Bought it at the hardware shop on Thursday afternoon, just in case.
F1
Wait—you were already planning a brand-new time capsule two days ago, {M1}?!
M1
That hollow pocket under the third courtyard stone is already lined with good brick.
F1
Seems a shame to leave good brick engineering empty for the next thirty years, right?
M1
Exactly my thought: pure practical maintenance, zero sentiment involved.
F1
Zero sentiment, says the man who already cut a fresh square of yellow beeswax linen!
M1
Watch your jokes, {F1}, or you will not get to write the lid label.
F1
Oh, please let me write the label! What year and message should we put on top?
M1
Write: Opened with friends in May—please open again thirty summers down the road.
F1
Who gets to choose what treasures go inside our new courtyard capsule tonight?
M1
Call {F2}, {F3}, and the brothers in here—everyone adds one honest piece of this week.
scenes.outro: Under the guise of pure brick maintenance, {M1} sparks a brand-new thirty-year courtyard tradition! See you next time.

scenes.title: Four Small Keepsakes
scenes.summary: Around the Room 9 table, F2, F3, and M4 place the complete laminated berry-cake recipe, the signed waltz sheet, wooden clothespin number 9, and a fresh group sketch into the new tin.
scenes.intro: Five minutes later around the glowing sunroom lamp, {F2}, {F3}, and {M4} gather over the open blue-and-brass tin box, each holding one small keepsake from their unforgettable week. Let us listen in first.
story: F2
First into the tin goes the COMPLETE berry almond cake recipe—both halves together!
M4
Did you seal it in waterproof plastic AND write HONEY AND ORANGE ZEST in capitals?!
F2
Future bakers thirty summers from tonight deserve zero ink smudges and zero soup ladles!
F3
Next, here is a clean signed copy of our Courtyard Waltz and four-hand duet.
M4
And from {M3} and me: birch clothespin number nine, signed on the back by everyone!
F2
Oh, look what our Room Eight mapmaker just sent in with {F3} to add on top!
F3
While we played piano, he sketched all twenty-eight of us under the rooftop lanterns!
M4
Look at {M1} standing by the doorway pretending not to smile in charcoal!
F2
Tuck a small packet of dried courtyard mint leaves in the corner for a sweet smell.
F3
Thirty summers from now, someone will lift this lid and smell warm summer tea.
M4
Lid pressed down snug, white cloth tape around the rim—ready for the waxed linen!
F2
Let us carry it out under the lanterns while the third stone is still waiting!
scenes.outro: A waterproof recipe, a rescued song, clothespin number nine, and a charcoal portrait rest safe inside the new tin! See you in the courtyard next time.

scenes.title: Back Under the Third Stone
scenes.summary: Under twenty-four glowing lanterns at twilight, M1, M2, and F1 lower the new waxed-cloth capsule into the brick pocket beneath the third flagstone north of the shade tree.
scenes.intro: Under twenty-four golden and coral rooftop lanterns, the courtyard grows hushed and warm as {M1}, {M2}, and {F1} kneel beside the third flat stone north of the old shade tree. Listen first.
story: M2
Everyone around the courtyard has their teacups raised—go ahead and place it in, {F1}.
F1
Wrapped tight in yellow waxed linen, resting dry and level on the clean river sand.
M1
Notice we kept the brass compass upstairs on the front desk where maps belong.
M2
And in its place, seven friends leave a warm hello for thirty summers ahead!
F1
Ready to slide the flat stone back over the brick pocket with {M1}, {M2}?
M1
Watch your fingers, boss—lower the north edge first, then let it settle flat.
M2
Not a wobble anywhere! Tap it once with your wooden handle for good luck, {M1}.
M1
Solid, level, and ready for table number one for the next thirty Mays.
F1
Look up through the tree branches at those rooftop lanterns shining against the evening sky!
M2
When Monday morning started two weeks ago, I worried about one swapped blue suitcase.
F1
Now look at {SHOW}: nine full rooms, twenty-eight neighbours, and music every week!
M1
Before you get misty-eyed again, boss, help me hang that framed map inside.
scenes.outro: The third courtyard stone settles home over a new thirty-year promise beneath the glowing lanterns. One final scene for Season 3—let us listen!

scenes.title: The Autumn Festival Envelope
scenes.summary: Hanging the framed watercolour map beside the front desk at nine in the evening, F1 and M2 discover an official municipal envelope from M4 inviting {SHOW} into the autumn Historic Courtyard Festival.
scenes.intro: At nine in the evening in the peaceful front lobby, the framed map of {STREET} hangs level beside hook number nine. {F1} and {M2} step back to admire it as {M4} leans against the counter hiding a wide grin. Listen first.
story: M2
Straight to the millimetre! Every guest who checks in will see {STREET} in gold leaf!
F1
Wait a minute, {M4}—why have you been grinning at your coat pocket for ten minutes?
M4
Because the Municipal Heritage Office asked me to hold one official letter until tonight!
M2
Official letter from City Hall?! Hold on, my heart cannot survive another inspection!
M4
Relax, {M2}—remember that Wednesday heritage report praising Room Nine and your courtyard?
F1
Look at the gold city crest on this cream envelope! Open it quickly, {M2}!
M2
Glasses on my nose—let me read: Invitation to the {CITY} Historic Courtyard Festival!
F1
THE HISTORIC COURTYARD FESTIVAL?! Five hidden courtyards opening across {CITY} for one weekend?!
M4
Music, baking, local craft tables, and a golden plaque for the warmest courtyard in town!
M2
Wait—hundreds of visitors walking down {STREET} for our piano and {F2} and her bread?!
F1
Say yes right now, {M2}—we already have windproof clothespins AND a master map!
M2
Dip the pen in ink, {F1}: {SHOW} is entering the Historic Courtyard Festival!
scenes.outro: The new time capsule rests beneath the tree, the golden map hangs beside hook number nine, and the Historic Courtyard Festival awaits! Season 3 of {SHOW} is complete—see you in Season 4!
